name: Toyota Safety Sense
summary: A family of Toyota active safety and driver-assistance systems.
how: Depending on the version and vehicle, cameras and other sensors support functions such as collision alerts and lane assistance. Check the specific system version and owner’s manual.
value: Helps explain the role of driver assistance in everyday driving without promising that every Toyota has the same functions.
limitations: The driver remains responsible for safe operation. Weather, road markings, visibility, and other conditions can limit performance. Contents vary by model and year.

name: IQ.DRIVE
summary: Volkswagen’s name for a suite of driver-assistance technologies.
how: Systems can assist with selected driving tasks using vehicle sensors. The exact functions and operating requirements must be checked for the vehicle and model year.
value: Provides a starting point for discussing support on the road, then demonstrating the actual vehicle’s controls.
limitations: Driver assistance does not replace an attentive driver. System availability and limitations vary; consult the owner’s manual.

name: Super Cruise
summary: GM’s hands-free driver-assistance technology for compatible roads and equipped vehicles.
how: Combines mapped-road information, sensors, and driver-attention monitoring. Confirm the vehicle’s hardware, service requirements, and road compatibility before describing operation.
value: Can reduce the effort of driving on supported roads while keeping the driver engaged.
limitations: It is not autonomous driving. An attentive driver is required. Road coverage, conditions, subscriptions, and vehicle eligibility apply.

name: Hybrid Synergy Drive
summary: Toyota terminology for an integrated gasoline-electric hybrid system.
how: An engine and electric motor system work together, with energy recovered during braking. Architecture and charging capability depend on the specific model; do not assume a hybrid is a plug-in.
value: Helps customers understand how gasoline and electric propulsion can work together in everyday use.
limitations: Efficiency varies with vehicle, weather, speed, and driving conditions. The name alone does not establish battery capacity, output, or electric range.

name: 4MOTION
how: The system manages drive torque to help traction. Its mechanical layout and operation depend on the vehicle and powertrain.
value: A practical way to introduce traction support and then explain the actual vehicle’s drive modes and tire requirements.
limitations: All-wheel drive does not remove the need for appropriate tires or safe driving, and it does not guarantee shorter braking distances. Availability varies by configuration.

name: Toyota Safety Sense 4.0 (2026 RAV4)
summary: The standard 2026 RAV4 suite includes pre-collision assistance, adaptive cruise control, lane assistance, automatic high beams, road-sign assistance and proactive driving support.
how: PCS can warn and may brake for certain potential frontal collisions. Full-Speed Range DRCC adjusts following distance; LTA helps center the vehicle while DRCC is engaged. LDA warns and may provide gentle steering support. AHB switches beams, RSA recognizes certain signs, and PDA can provide gentle braking or steering support.
value: Demonstrate the actual controls and explain how several systems support everyday driving; do not describe the suite as autonomous driving.
limitations: Road, weather, light, markings, object position and vehicle conditions can limit operation. The driver remains responsible. Consult the exact owner’s manual. TSS 4.0 is distinct from the optional/grade-dependent Traffic Jam Assist and Advanced Park features.

name: Electronic On-Demand AWD (2026 RAV4)
summary: An electric rear motor provides rear-wheel drive assistance on AWD configurations.
how: Vehicle sensors and driver inputs are used to control front/rear torque distribution. The rear motor can assist during acceleration or when front-wheel slip is detected.
value: Useful for a customer considering traction support; contrast the exact FWD and AWD configurations and their verified output and towing ratings.
limitations: It does not replace appropriate tires or attentive driving. Availability, output and equipment must be checked for the actual configuration; do not promise a towing capacity based only on the AWD badge.

name: RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid charging (2026)
summary: The four PHEV grades do not all use the same charging hardware.
how: Toyota lists 7-kW onboard AC charging with J1772 for SE and GR SPORT, and 11-kW onboard AC charging with a CCS1 port and DC capability for XSE and Woodland. The release estimates 10–80% around four hours on Level 2 for the AC-only pair, and around 30 minutes on DC for the CCS1 pair under ideal conditions.
value: Ask about home charging and travel needs before recommending a grade. Explain why moving to a sport-oriented GR SPORT does not also add DC charging.
limitations: Charger compatibility, temperature, battery condition and other factors affect time and range. The times are manufacturer estimates for different charging methods, not directly interchangeable tests. The HEV brochure is not a PHEV charging specification.

name: Toyota Audio Multimedia (2026 RAV4)
summary: The HEV brochure specifies 10.5-inch screens on LE, SE, XLE Premium and Woodland, and 12.9-inch screens on XSE and Limited.
how: Touch and voice functions bring audio and compatible phone features into the cabin. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard in the HEV matrix. The 12.3-inch instrument cluster is a separate display.
value: Separate screen size from speaker equipment: HEV XSE has six speakers as standard, Limited has nine-speaker JBL; the XSE JBL package is named but its exact contents are not itemized.
limitations: Compatible devices and services are required. Connected features can require account setup, connectivity, trials or subscriptions. Do not transfer the HEV screen/audio matrix to PHEV grades.

name: Traffic Jam Assist (2026 RAV4)
summary: The HEV table marks it available on XLE Premium and standard on Woodland, XSE and Limited.
how: The brochure describes support for stop-and-go driving on controlled-access highways at 25 mph or less, with Lane Tracing Assist active. The driver must supervise the system at all times.
value: Explain its intended traffic conditions and service requirements before demonstrating it.
limitations: An active Drive Connect trial/subscription is required. Account setup and network availability apply. It is not automated driving. The brochure’s network wording varies between its overview and footnote; confirm current service availability.

name: Blind Spot Monitor, RCTA & Safe Exit Alert (2026 RAV4 HEV)
summary: The HEV equipment matrix lists Blind Spot Monitor, Rear Cross-Traffic Alert and Safe Exit Alert as standard on all six grades.
how: BSM warns about vehicles in a blind spot; RCTA helps detect vehicles approaching from the sides while reversing. Safe Exit Alert can warn about approaching vehicles or cyclists when a door is opening.
value: Three practical scenarios make the feature set easy to explain: lane changes, backing out of a space and opening a door.
limitations: Warnings do not guarantee detection or clearance. Check surroundings directly and consult the owner’s manual; Safe Exit Alert is not a promise that a door cannot open.

name: Panoramic View Monitor & Multi-Terrain Monitor (2026 RAV4 HEV)
summary: The HEV brochure lists PVM as standard on Woodland, XSE and Limited; Woodland also has Multi-Terrain Monitor.
how: PVM provides a 3D 360-degree overhead view in low-speed drive and reverse, plus curb view. Woodland’s MTM offers selectable front, side and rear views.
value: Camera views can help a customer understand clearances when parking or viewing uneven terrain.
limitations: Cameras do not show every object or the entire surrounding area. Look directly around the vehicle and follow the owner’s manual. No PHEV availability is inferred from this HEV table.

name: Advanced Park (2026 RAV4 HEV)
summary: The HEV table marks Advanced Park standard on Limited and available on XSE.
how: The brochure describes button-activated parking assistance. Demonstrate only according to the actual vehicle’s owner’s manual and operating requirements.
value: A useful convenience distinction when comparing HEV Limited with XSE; optional XSE availability is not the same as equipment installed on the vehicle.
limitations: Remain attentive to surroundings. The reviewed brochure does not itemize the XSE package’s contents, so do not promise a complete package bundle from this availability mark.
